briefing.headline: OpenAI Orion-2 and xAI Colossus-3 accelerate AGI timelines as compute shortages intensify

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: Frontier labs released multiple high-capability models this quarter, pushing benchmark saturation on agentic tasks. Funding remains robust despite regulatory scrutiny in the US and EU. Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability across deployed systems.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI launched Orion-2 with improved long-horizon reasoning; Anthropic's Claude 4 Opus and Google's Gemini 3 Ultra both set new records on SWE-bench. Meta open-sourced Llama 4 405B while DeepSeek-R2 closed the gap on Western labs.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems and that DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level. NIST and EU AI Office issued joint guidance on multi-agent security testing.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: TSMC began volume production of 1.4nm AI chips; Microsoft and CoreWeave announced 200k H200 cluster expansions. Energy constraints are forcing new data center locations in Canada and Nordic regions.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will the first system to achieve 90% on the ARC-AGI benchmark trigger immediate international compute-sharing agreements?
